title: Exact prefetch helped a narrow long-context case but did not generalize
summary: The 1.5B long-context study saved 426.5 MiB of peak CUDA allocation relative to large-cache ARC while remaining within 1% throughput in all six pairs. At equal smaller budgets it was 1.36% faster with much shorter return latency; the short-context case missed the large-ARC throughput target.
scope: RTX 2080 Ti/WSL, FP16 Qwen2.5-1.5B, three content seeds with two balanced repetitions, long and short tool-return workloads. Forty-two confirmation runs passed exact prompt/output/native-key/physical checks.
limitations: Return latency still rose 25.1 ms against large-cache ARC. Performance runs had zero constrained semantic choices. Separate intrusive diagnostics found only 2/5 top-choice agreement with the old EMA policy. A later non-restoring ARC control diverged in output, with no established cause.
decision: Preserve this scoped positive alongside later public-workload negatives. Configured KV-pool reduction is not a general memory efficiency claim; ranking and output-repeatability questions remain open.
